{{Expand Japanese|天孫族}}

{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|Tenson-zoku}} (天孫族) is a generic term for ancient people that established the {{ill|Yamato kingship|en|Yamato kingship}}, which appears in the [[Kojiki]] and the [[Nihon Shoki]] and which is told in Japanese mythology. The ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku}}'' defines "Tenson" as the offspring of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|Amenohoakari}}<ref name="yu-2023a" /> who it identifies with {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|fr|Nigihayahi}}.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Shoki Mononobe-uji no Keifu (1) Kokigi no Heya (初期物部氏の系譜 (1) 古樹紀之房間)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2007|location=Japan}}</ref> It mentions that the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|en|Imperial House of Japan|qid=Q909452|lt=Imperial Family}}, the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|Mononobe clan}} and an ancient tribe of {{ill|Hayato people|en|fr|Hayato|Hayato people|lt=Hayato}} descended from the Tenson tribe.<ref name="yu-2023a">{{Cite web|last=Yu|first=A. C.|title=Tenson-zoku (Tenson Tribe) - Japanese Wiki Corpus|url=https://www.japanesewiki.com/literature/Tenson-zoku%20(Tenson%20Tribe).html|access-date=2023-12-11|website=www.japanesewiki.com|publisher={{ill|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology|en|National Institute of Information and Communications Technology}}}}</ref>

The Tenson tribe descended from [[Takamagahara|Takamagahara]] to conquer {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ashihara no Nakatsukuni|en|fr}}'''|葦原の中つ国|''The middle country of {{ill|reed bed|en|reed bed|lt=reed beds}}''}} in the [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]] region. Vanquishing the ruling families across western Japan they established the {{ill|List of emperors of Japan|en|List of emperors of Japan|qid=Q188210|lt=Yamato dynasty}} ({{ill|Wakoku|en|Wakoku}}) which was ruled by the {{ill|Okimi|en|Okimi|lt=Great King of Yamato}} ({{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|qid=Q208233|lt=emperor}}). The dynasty expanded its power to {{ill|Chūbu region|en|Chūbu region|qid=Q134638|lt=Chubu}} and {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|qid=Q132480|lt=Kanto}} regions and developed into Japan as we know it today.<ref name="yu-2023a" />
== Genealogy ==
The {{nihongo|Amabe clan genealogy|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu||draft}} is a famous document housed at Kono Shrine. It is from early {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan. The clan claims descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|Amenohoakari}}, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko|kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of {{ill|Tanba Province|en|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba Province}} before it was divided into Tanba and Tango. The document records 82 generations of descent from {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|Amenohoakari}}. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|publisher={{ill|Agency for Cultural Affairs|en|Agency for Cultural Affairs}}|language=Japanese|accessdate=August 20, 2020|qq=draft}}</ref>

In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku}}'', the descendants of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|en|Amatsuhikone}}, {{ill|Ame no Hohi|en|Ame no Hohi}}, and {{ill|Amanomichine|ja|天道根命|en:draft|Amanomichine}}, together with the descendants of Amenohoakari are referred to as {{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}} (天孫族). The ''{{ill|Tenson-zoku|fr|ja|天孫族|zh|天孫民族|en:draft|ko|천손족|uk|Тенсон Зоку}}'' descended from [[Takamagahara]] (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|Heaven}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|lt=Owari}} and {{ill|Tanba Province|en|Tanba Province|lt=Tanba}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of {{ill|Owari clan|en|fr|clan Owari|Owari clan|lt=Owari}}, {{ill|Tsumori clan|ja|津守氏|en|Tsumori clan|lt=Tsumori}}, {{ill|Amabe clan|en|Amabe clan|qid=Q65272445|lt=Amabe}}, and {{ill|Tanba clan|ja|丹波氏|en|Tanba clan|lt=Tanba}} clans.<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242|title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄)|last=Hanawa|first=Hokiichi|date=1983|publisher=Onkogakkai|location=Japan|oclc=959773242|en}}</ref>

However, it is clear that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of {{ill|Amenohoakari|en|Amenohoakari}}, is a forged document, and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|en|List of water deities|lt=sea deity}} {{ill|Watatsumi|en|Watatsumi|qid=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi}}. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, {{ill|Takakuraji|fr|Takakuraji|ja|高倉下|zh|高倉下|qid=Q11668757|lt=Takakuraji}}, as their ancestor, and this is considered to be the original genealogy.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族)|last=Hoga|first=Toshio|year=2006|location=Japan}}</ref>
